title: Cloud Vendor Integrations: Launch Brief & Listing Readiness (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working launch brief to prepare a cloud vendor marketplace listing for a partner integration (AWS/Azure/GCP). It combines suggested marketing copy, technical and commercial readiness checklist, and a proposed go/no-go QA matrix. Treat as a living doc — most items are TODOs or assumptions that need confirmation from engineering, legal, and partner contacts.

TL;DR (one-paragraph):
Redwood Inference is launching a marketplace listing that enables customers to provision hosted inference with predictable performance and enterprise controls via their cloud vendor of choice. Listing will highlight: predictable pricing tiers (hosted + dedicated), private deployment options, KMS/HSM integrations, and SSO + audit logs. Target launch window: H1 2025; gating items: billing SKU setup, security review, and partner co-brand assets.

Audience and success metrics:
- Primary audience: Platform engineers, AI/ML teams evaluating managed inference for production workloads.
- Success metrics (first 90 days): 250 trial signups via listing, 20 demo requests, 2 pilot contracts (Dedicated) signed.

Suggested listing copy variants (short + long + bullets) - use these in vendor portals where char limits differ:
1) Short headline (<= 80 chars):
- "High-performance LLM inference: predictable latency, lower unit cost"

2) 1-line elevator (cloud portal summary):
- "Run production-grade LLM inference with transparent performance and options for hosted, dedicated, or private deployments."

3) Long description (for marketplace detail page):
- "Redwood Inference delivers a unified runtime for serving LLMs at production scale. Choose hosted API for fast time-to-value, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, or private deployment for regulated workloads. Our runtime focuses on reducing per-token cost (intelligent batching, KV caching, quantization recommendations) while delivering SLO-backed latency and enterprise observability. Integrates with KMS, single sign-on (SAML/OIDC), and cloud billing for simplified procurement and management."

4) Feature bullets (short form for tile/grid):
- Hosted API: immediate access to curated open models and streaming responses
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools, autoscaling, SLA-backed latency targets
- Private deployments: VPC and on-prem install options, audit logs, KMS support
- Cost controls: batching and quantization suggestions, per-token cost breakouts
- Observability: per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, error analysis

5) Call-to-action variants (for button text):
- "Start free trial" / "Request Dedicated Demo" / "Contact sales for Private"

Marketing asset notes (assets we need from partner + our assets):
- Partner: co-brand logo (SVG), approved partner blurb, customer reference permission (if available)
- Redwood: 1-min product video clip, 3 screenshots (console + metrics), 2 short customer blurbs, pricing tier copy, support SLA blurb
- Legal: approved listing terms and allowed marketing claims

Technical & ops readiness checklist (must confirm before listing goes live):
- Billing SKUs created and linked to cloud vendor listing (action: Finance)
- Marketplace billing integration tested end-to-end (procurement -> metering) (action: infra/finance)
- Valid product ID and entitlements mapping for trial vs paid tiers (action: product)
- SSO integrations documented and tested (SAML/OIDC) (action: engineering)
- KMS/HSM support documented; key management workflow tested (action: security)
- Deployment artifacts for private/VPC options uploaded to partner portal (action: private-deployments eng)
- Customer onboarding flow documented (console invite, entitlement assignment, initial quota) (action: dx)
- Support routing: marketplace cases triaged to CS + GTM escalation path defined (action: customer-success)
- Compliance checklist passed (SOC2/ISO summary, privacy matrix) and allowed to be displayed in listing (action: security/compliance)
- Pricing table and unit economics verified (unit token pricing, rounding rules, minimum commitments) (action: finance/product)

QA acceptance matrix (working):
- Billing: create test purchase via vendor portal -> confirm Redwood billing event (PASS/FAIL)
- Provisioning: buyer creates account via portal -> receives API key and sandbox access (PASS/FAIL)
- Latency assertion: sample benchmark page shows median latency under declared SLO for small model (PASS/FAIL)
- Trial entitlement enforcement: trial limits enforced in console and via API (PASS/FAIL)
- Private deployment option: partner provisioning playbook present (PASS/FAIL)
- Observability: example console metrics render and token usage tracked per-route (PASS/FAIL)

Launch scenarios and gating:
- Soft launch (limited visibility): publish listing in vendor sandbox + private link to pilot customers — good for early buyer feedback and clearing billing edge cases.
- Public launch: listing public in marketplace, marketing email + social amplification. Gate: billing + security + 3 pilot customers successfully onboarded.

Commercial terms and decision points (items to clarify with Finance/Legal):
- How to present free tier vs trial phrasing in marketplace copy (free trial of hosted API vs free-tier limited credits).
- Contract flow for Dedicated and Private: standard marketplace procurement vs separate MSA + SOW. Must include allowed procurement patterns in listing docs.
- Refund and cancellation policy for marketplace purchases.

Open questions / assumptions (action owners in parens):
- Do we want to list Dedicated as a purchasable SKU or as "contact sales" only? (Product/Finance)
- Do partner portals allow embedding performance numbers (latency percentiles) or only qualitative claims? (GTM/Sales)
- Can we show third-party compliance badges on the listing page or do we need partner approval? (Security/Legal)
- Are there Marketplace-specific terms that conflict with Redwood commercial language (e.g., auto-renewal, cancellation)? (Legal)

Acceptance copy snippets for partner review (quick samples to send to partner for approval):
- "Redwood Inference (hosted) gives teams a predictable, production-ready inference platform with per-route cost visibility and SLA-backed latency. Available as a hosted API, reserved dedicated capacity, or private deployment behind your VPC."
- "Deploy high-throughput LLM inference without managing GPU fleets — Redwood handles batching, caching, and kernel selection while you focus on product features."

Go-to-market checklist (timeline + owners):
- Week -6: Finalize copy and creative assets (Owner: Marketing - Maya)
- Week -4: Billing SKUs & sandbox testing (Owner: Finance - Ethan)
- Week -3: Security signoff + compliance badge permission (Owner: Security - Priya)
- Week -2: Pilot onboarding + QA matrix completion (Owner: Solutions Eng)
- Week 0: Publish listing (Owner: GTM launch lead)

Next steps (immediate):
- [ ] Confirm billing SKU naming convention and create initial test SKUs (Ethan)
- [ ] Send copy drafts to partner for brand approval (Noah/Maya)
- [ ] Open Jira epic GTM-982 and assign tasks to infra, security, and dx (Noah)
- [ ] Schedule sandbox test run with partner technical contact (Priya)

Notes to self / working fragments (rough):
- Consider a short "cost-savings" calculator tile in listing that shows estimated cost-per-1M tokens for different configurations. Might be heavy for marketplace UI but useful for link-to calculator.
- If partner requires co-selling language, prepare a one-pager with lead routing and referral credits.
- Keep copy modular so we can swap short vs long descriptions into different vendor character limits.

Revision history:
- 2025-01-07 Noah Patel: initial draft
- 2025-01-21 Maya Li: added marketing asset list + CTA variants
- 2025-02-14 Priya Sharma: updated technical checklist and dates

Attachments (to upload to vendor portal when ready):
- product-video-60s.mp4 (hosted link)
- screenshots: console-metrics.png, listing-tiles.png, onboarding-flow.png
- legal: marketplace-terms-approved.pdf

End of brief.
